correctness.rationale: For distinct scores the full graph support is the extreme range; suppressing its extremal edge forces at least the lesser endpoint gap loss. A deleted matching retains both next-best extremal alternatives and attains this bound pointwise. Exchangeability independently randomizes extreme-label edge and ordered spacings, giving the exact Bernoulli mixture. A shared missing endpoint gives an open strictly worse event. Gaussian radial projection supplies exact intrinsic chi_(n-1) normalization. Layer-cake order-statistic integration yields the stated positive Gaussian constant; independent upper/lower Poisson extreme limits and a hazard-rate/tail bound ensure asymptotic expectation convergence. The embedded checker exhausts 651 small deleted-edge sets and all value-order permutations, plus a seeded uniform benchmark; this is corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Euclidean mean width is the first intrinsic volume up to a standard factor, and densely connected signed-root polytopes provide a natural graph-convex-geometric family. With the same n and deletion budget k, all graphs have exactly the same probability that the globally maximizing edge was removed, yet the full severity distribution differs; the theorem classifies matching deletion as the unique minimizer for every i.i.d. continuous score law. Its sharp, nontrivial n- and k-dependent width decrement and extreme-value constant quantify this protection even when the matching removes the largest admissible number of edges. Neither face counts, an inradius, or a generic Gaussian formula answer that extremal geometric-design question.
